heads.en: Exposition on the Song of Songs

headnotes.la: …a sum, cessent legati; jam ipse veniat, manifestetur, figat oscula, det amplexus, proprioque ore mihi loquatur. Apostropha. Te, inquit, diligo, et desidero, te audire, te videre concupisco. Quare hoc?
headnotes.en: … manifest, let him fasten kisses upon me, let him give embraces, and let him speak to me with his own mouth. Apostrophe. Thee, she says, I love, and I desire; I long to hear thee, to see thee. Why so?

headnotes.la: …o, et exponendo, lacteam, dulcemque suavitatem retraxit. Quos enim lex occidere videbat, ipse misericorditer sanabat. Mulierem namque in adulterio deprehensam Judaei lapidare volebant, Christus autem,
headnotes.en: …by teaching and expounding, drew back a milky and sweet suavity. For those whom the law looked to slay, he mercifully healed. For the Jews wished to stone the woman taken in adultery, but Christ said,

headnotes.la: inquit. Sunt autem haec verba vino meliora
headnotes.en: And these words are better than wine

headnotes.la: …ti? His autem fragrant, splendent, et redolent et novum et vetus testamentum. Hunc odorem Christi praedicatio inferebat; quoniam alios sapientes, alios intelligentes, alios fortes, alios pios faciebat
headnotes.en: …New and the Old Testament are fragrant, and shine, and give forth their scent. This odor the preaching of Christ brought in, since it made some wise, others understanding, others strong, others devout

headnotes.la: Per aromata quidem quascunque res odoriferas intelligimus. Sed quid tanti odoris, tantaeque suavitatis, ut ipse spiritus esse possit, quo Apostolus repletus dicebat
headnotes.en: By the spices we understand whatever things are odor-bearing. But what could be of so great an odor and so great a sweetness that it might be the Spirit himself, filled with whom the Apostle said

headnotes.la: [n: (II Cor. II, 15.)] Vox Ecclesiae ad Christum
headnotes.en: [n: (II Cor. II, 15.)] The voice of the Church to Christ

headnotes.la: …s praebuit sanitatem. Christus namque a chrismate dicitur, in quo nomine baptismatis aqua mundati omnes Christiani vocamur. Hoc igitur nomen super electos diffusum Spiritus sancti gratia eos conjunxit
headnotes.en: …from the chrism, in which name we are all called Christians, cleansed by the water of baptism. This name, therefore, poured out over the elect, has joined them together by the grace of the Holy Spirit

headnotes.la: Post se namque Christus eos trahit, quicunque eum imitantur, ut qui ipsius imperio super coelos exaltantur
headnotes.en: For Christ draws after himself whoever imitate him, so that they who are exalted above the heavens by his own command

headnotes.la: Ipse quidem per se ascendit, qui et perfectus *606* Deus est, et perfectus homo. Caeteri autem, quoniam per se ascendere nequeunt, ut trahantur, necesse est. Trahuntur igitur, sicut ipse Dominus ait
headnotes.en: …ndeed ascended by himself, who is both perfect *606* God and perfect man. But the rest, since they cannot ascend by themselves, must needs be drawn. They are drawn, therefore, as the Lord himself says

headnotes.la: …atiarum. In istarum namque odorem currunt, qui earum suavitate et dulcedine capti incessanter bona operantur. Qui enim vitiis foetent, eis quidem haec omnia non redolent. Vox sponsae ad adolescentulas
headnotes.en: …ivated by their sweetness and delight, work good things without ceasing. But those who stink with vices — to them indeed all these things give no fragrance. The voice of the bride to the young maidens

headnotes.la: … in aeterna tabernacula fide et spe me Rex regum introduxit. Possumus etiam per cellaria singulos prophetarum libros intelligere, in quos Ecclesia introducta spirituali vino inebriatur. Unde Psalmista
headnotes.en: …nto the eternal tabernacles. We may also understand by the storerooms the several books of the prophets, into which the Church, being brought in, is made drunk with spiritual wine. Whence the Psalmist

headnotes.la: Apostropha
headnotes.en: Apostrophe

headnotes.la: …voluminibus ecclesiastici viri reperiunt, in tanto talique viro exsultant, et laetantur. Denique cum ad summam illam beatitudinem pervenerunt, summis et aeternis bonis receptis, in eo solo exsultabunt
headnotes.en: …ed volumes, they exult and rejoice in so great and such a man. And at last, when they have come to that highest blessedness, having received the highest and eternal goods, they will exult in him alone

headnotes.la: …super vinum, venit Novum Testamentum super Vetus; temperatum est vinum, dulcis, mitis, et intelligibilis facta est lex. Consummatum est igitur super domum Israel, et super domum Juda Testamentum Novum
headnotes.en: …stament came above the Old; the wine was tempered, and the law was made sweet, mild, and intelligible. The New Testament, therefore, was consummated over the house of Israel and over the house of Juda

headnotes.la: …ur. Reges enim sunt apostoli, episcopi, et sacerdotes. Apostoli autem nisi Christum diligerent, pro eo quidem non morerentur. Diligunt igitur reges et recti, a quo fiunt reges, et recti. Vox synagogae
headnotes.en: …kings. And unless the apostles had loved Christ, they would not indeed have died for him. Therefore kings and upright men love him from whom they are made kings and upright. The voice of the synagogue

headnotes.la: …it. Vos, inquit, filiae Jerusalem, filiae Libani, filiae candidationis estis. Ego autem filia Cedar, filia tenebrarum, filia cervorum fui. Ego populus, qui sedebat in tenebris. Ego sum, cui dictum est
headnotes.en: …alem, daughters of Libanus, daughters of whitening. But I was the daughter of Cedar, the daughter of darkness, the daughter of stags. I am the people that sat in darkness. I am she to whom it was said

headnotes.la: Consentio igitur, quia nigra sum, quoniam in peccatis nata sum: secundum creationem, pristinamque vitam nigra; secundum regenerationem autem super nivem dealbata
headnotes.en: I grant, therefore, that I am black, since I was born in sins: black according to my creation and my former life, but according to my regeneration made whiter than snow

headnotes.la: …a? In oculis, in auribus, omnibusque membris. Deformes enim oculi sunt, quod deformia et turpia videre concupiscunt; deformes aures, quod vaniloquia, et scurrilitatem audire delectantur. E contra vero
headnotes.en: …n my ears, and in all my members. For eyes are uncomely in that they long to see uncomely and base things; ears are uncomely in that they delight to hear vain talk and buffoonery. But on the contrary,

headnotes.la: Cedar *tenebrae* interpretatur. Tenebrarum vero nigredo sola luce fugatur. Erat igitur Ecclesia nigra sicut tabernacula Cedar, quae a sole justitiae illuminata candida facta est. Unde Evangelista
headnotes.en: … the blackness of darkness is put to flight by light alone. The Church, then, was black as the tabernacles of Cedar, and being illumined by the sun of justice she was made white. Whence the Evangelist

headnotes.la: Cedar quidem tabernacula sunt, in quibus tenebrarum principes inhabitant. Denique secundum carnem non majoris pulchritudinis sunt justi quam injusti
headnotes.en: The tabernacles of Cedar are indeed those in which the princes of darkness dwell. And in short, according to the flesh the just are of no greater beauty than the unjust

headnotes.la: …a vero sicut pelles Salomonis. Non me igitur despiciat Salomon; si quidem mea pellis pelli suae convenit. Est igitur Ecclesia inter mulieres speciosa, atque formosa, quoniam quidem praedictus Salomon,
headnotes.en: …edar, but comely as the skins of Solomon. Let not Solomon therefore despise me, since my skin agrees with his skin. The Church, then, is fair and comely among women, since indeed the aforesaid Solomon

headnotes.la: Vox Ecclesiae
headnotes.en: The voice of the Church

headnotes.la: …mbra quievi, non in lecto me otio dedi. Quid igitur? In vinea laboravi, agrum excolui, vigilavi, jejunavi, sole insuper multas adversitates perpessa decolorata sum, et fusca. Quid mirum? Vox Synagogae
headnotes.en: … the vineyard, I tilled the field, I kept watch, I fasted; and moreover, having endured many adversities under the sun, I have been discolored and made swarthy. What wonder? The voice of the Synagogue

headnotes.la: …tris meae mihi bellum inferebant. Foris igitur pugnae, intus timores, hinc tyrannorum gladius, hinc Judaeorum, et haereticorum disputatio. Matrem suam Judaeam, vel synagogam intelligas. Unde Apostolus
headnotes.en: …e fightings; within, fears; on this side the sword of tyrants, on that the disputation of the Jews and of the heretics. You may understand her mother to be Judaea, or the synagogue. Whence the Apostle

headnotes.la: etc. Possumus autem per hanc matrem, iniquitatem intelligere. Unde Psalmista
headnotes.en: etc. But we may also understand by this mother iniquity. Whence the Psalmist

headnotes.la: Quis igitur, nisi pro arcendis furibus ponit in vineis custodes? Unam Deus vineam plantavit, quae quoniam in amaritudinem conversa est, multae aliae vineae plantatae sunt. Unde et illud
headnotes.en: Who, then, sets keepers in the vineyards, except to ward off thieves? God planted one vineyard, and because it was turned into bitterness, many other vineyards were planted. Whence also that saying

headnotes.la: In his apostoli positi sunt custodes, ne eam vindemiarent omnes qui praetergrediuntur viam
headnotes.en: In these the apostles were set as keepers, lest all they that pass by the way should gather her vintage

headnotes.la: Vineam, inquit, unam reliqui, vineas autem multas custodivi. Multae autem vineae multae sunt Ecclesiae. Una vero synagoga est. Hanc autem reliquerunt apostoli, sicut scriptum est
headnotes.en: One vineyard, she says, I have left, but many vineyards I have kept. And the many vineyards are the many churches. But the synagogue is one. And the apostles left her, as it is written

headnotes.la: … una est. Hanc autem custodierunt apostoli et doctores, ne Arius, Sabellius, caeterique fures aliquem dolose racemum subriperent, neve quemque fidelem ab Ecclesia separarent. Vox Ecclesiae ad Christum
headnotes.en: …ostles and the doctors kept it, lest Arius, Sabellius, and the other thieves should craftily steal away some cluster, or separate any of the faithful from the Church. The voice of the Church to Christ

headnotes.la: …nutrias. Dei namque oves in conventu praedicationis, et sacris voluminibus pascuntur. Illis autem episcopis etiam indicatum est, qui canes muti non latrare valentes, Dei animalia fame perire patiuntur
headnotes.en: … God's sheep are fed in the assembly of preaching and in the sacred volumes. And this has been shown also to those bishops who, being dumb dogs unable to bark, suffer God's animals to perish of hunger

headnotes.la: …aniantur? Nonne tu es ille qui, ut bonus pastor, animam pro ovibus ponis? Gravis est aestus, sitiunt oves, uruntur calore. Duc ad portum, duc ad umbram. Scio; dices: In te sum, in te cubo et requiesco
headnotes.en: …e for the sheep? The heat is heavy, the sheep thirst, they are burned with the warmth. Lead them to the harbor, lead them to the shade. I know; thou wilt say: I am in thee, in thee I lie down and rest

headnotes.la: [n: (Isa, LVI, 2.)] Itemque
headnotes.en: [n: (Isa, LVI, 2.)] And likewise

headnotes.la: …ltas tribulationes oportet nos intrare in regna coelorum. Vera est responsio; jam nihil timeo; siquidem tantus hospes civitatem custodit. Aestum non perhorresco, quoniam fons vivus mecum est. Sequitur
headnotes.en: …ust enter into the kingdoms of heaven. The answer is true; now I fear nothing, since so great a guest guards the city. I do not shudder at the heat, since the living fountain is with me. There follows

headnotes.la: Vox Christi ad Ecclesiam
headnotes.en: The voice of Christ to the Church

headnotes.la: …que hircos convertimus. Hi autem haedi juxta pastorum tabernacula, et haereticorum conventicula, suavi Scripturarum cibo fastidito, venenosa pascuntur herba, id est prava dogmata hauriunt. Vox Christi
headnotes.en: …les of the shepherds and the conventicles of the heretics, having scorned the sweet food of the Scriptures, are fed with poisonous grass, that is, they drink in depraved teachings. The voice of Christ

headnotes.la: His autem quasi exprobrationis verbis auditis, propter verba superius dicta, verecundiae sibi attraxit ruborem. Dixerat enim
headnotes.en: But when she had heard these words, as it were of rebuke, on account of the words spoken above, she drew upon herself the blush of shame. For she had said,

headnotes.la: Vagari namque meretricum est. Hujus igitur verbi hujusque temeritatis recordata erubuit. Sponsus autem, haec ut vidit, virginalem verecundiam laudavit. Ait enim
headnotes.en: For wandering belongs to harlots. Recalling therefore this word and this rashness, she blushed. But the Bridegroom, when he saw this, praised her virginal modesty. For he says

headnotes.la: … ex illis non es, quae a crimine vires sumunt. Sed quomodo pulchrae? Sicut turturis, sicut virginis, sicut magnae castitatis et conjugalis fidei observatricis. Non enim nisi uni Ecclesia servit marito
headnotes.en: …f those women who take their strength from crime. But how beautiful? As the turtledove's, as a virgin's, as of one who keeps great chastity and conjugal faith. For the Church serves no husband but one

headnotes.la: …bus immittitur, de quo et verba exeunt. Ecclesia vero a doctoribus nutritur et eruditur. Colli igitur officium a doctoribus expletur. Praeterea colli infirmitas totius corporis est ruina. Vox amicorum
headnotes.en: …h is nourished and instructed by the doctors. The office of the neck, therefore, is fulfilled by the doctors. Moreover, the weakness of the neck is the ruin of the whole body. The voice of the friends

headnotes.la: …uncupatae. Significant autem sermones prophetarum prolixos, et dictinctos, et laudabiles. Murenulas nobis Moyses, Isaias, Jeremias, David, et hic quidem, qui haec scripsit Ecclesiastes, nobis fecerunt
headnotes.en: …e discourses of the prophets, lengthy, and [sic: *dictinctos*], and praiseworthy. *Murenulae* were made for us by Moses, Isaias, Jeremias, David, and by him indeed who wrote these things, Ecclesiastes

headnotes.la: Vox sponsae
headnotes.en: The voice of the bride

headnotes.la: Cum, inquit, rex meus, sponsus meus, dilectus meus esset in accubitu, in lectulo carnis, in humanitate, quam ex virginali utero assumpsit,
headnotes.en: While my king, she says, my bridegroom, my beloved, was at his repose, upon the little bed of the flesh, in the humanity which he took from a virginal womb,

headnotes.la: …ucorum virtutes, et orationes Domino placebant. Postquam autem in carnem venit, et tanquam sponsus de thalamo suo Dominus processit, mox sanctorum virtutes et orationes odorem dederunt. Unde Apostolus
headnotes.en: …ing to the Lord. But after he came in the flesh, and the Lord went forth as a bridegroom out of his chamber, straightway the virtues and prayers of the saints gave forth their odor. Whence the Apostle

headnotes.la: Et Psalmista
headnotes.en: And the Psalmist

headnotes.la: …oannes phialas aureas odoramentorum plenas vidit [n: (Apoc. V, 8)]. Post Christi namque incarnationem, et virtus sanctorum, et numerus crevit. Dedit igitur *609* nardus odorem Christo Domino incarnato
headnotes.en: … [n: (Apoc. V, 8)]. For after the incarnation of Christ both the virtue of the saints and their number increased. The nard therefore gave *609* forth its odor to Christ the Lord when he was made flesh

headnotes.la: …tus Ecclesiae myrrhae fasciculus; et quidem magni doloris, magnaeque amaritudinis collectio. Quomodo enim nisi in dolore et amaritudine esse poterat, tanto talique viduata viro? Sic quoque dici potest
headnotes.en: … bundle of myrrh, and indeed a gathering of great grief and great bitterness. For how could she be otherwise than in grief and bitterness, widowed of so great and such a husband? So too it can be said

headnotes.la: Propter me, meique ad utilitatem fasciculus myrrhae factus est, quoniam morti et passionis amaritudini sese pro me subdidit. Nonne myrrhae et amaritudinis portabat fasciculum, cum diceret
headnotes.en: …e and for my profit was he made a bundle of myrrh, since he submitted himself for me to death and to the bitterness of the passion. Was he not carrying a bundle of myrrh and of bitterness when he said

headnotes.la: …tem fasciculus myrrhae factus est, quoniam morti et passionis amaritudini sese pro me subdidit. Nonne myrrhae et amaritudinis portabat fasciculum, cum diceret: « Tristis est anima mea usque ad mortem?
headnotes.en: …of myrrh, since he submitted himself for me to death and to the bitterness of the passion. Was he not carrying a bundle of myrrh and of bitterness when he said: « My soul is sorrowful even unto death?

headnotes.la: …nima mea usque ad mortem? « [n: (Matth. XXVI, 38.)] Fuit equidem fasciculus, quia et multos ad se traxit, et multos secum occidit. Omnes enim martyres pro morte ipsius, quasi uno fasciculo colliguntur
headnotes.en: …to death? « [n: (Matth. XXVI, 38.)] He was indeed a bundle, because he both drew many to himself and slew many with himself. For all the martyrs are gathered, as it were into one bundle, for his death

headnotes.la: …r ubera commoratur, siquidem in corde jacet, memoriam fugere nequit. Felix illa anima, nimiumque felix, cujus inter ubera Christus commoratur, cujus in corde jacet, et quae ipsius nunquam obliviscitur
headnotes.en: …een the breasts, since he lies in the heart, cannot escape the memory. Happy is that soul, and exceedingly happy, between whose breasts Christ abides, in whose heart he lies, and who never forgets him

headnotes.la: …is suis botrus Cypri, quoniam ejus sanguinis haustu laetificantur. Denique si vinum laetitiam significat, merito qui fuerat fasciculus myrrhae moriendo, botrus Cypri dicitur resurgendo. Unde Psalmista
headnotes.en: …ddened by the draught of his blood. And in short, if wine signifies gladness, then he who had been a bundle of myrrh in dying is rightly called a cluster of Cyprus in rising again. Whence the Psalmist

headnotes.la: Est igitur botrus Cypri. Ubi? Sequitur
headnotes.en: He is therefore a cluster of Cyprus. Where? There follows

headnotes.la: Vox Christi
headnotes.en: The voice of Christ

headnotes.la: Confirmatio
headnotes.en: Confirmation

headnotes.la: Pulchra, inquit, es, sine macula es, interius exteriusque casta es. Magnae enim inter Christum et Ecclesiam sunt amicitiae; cum et Christus pro Ecelesia, et Ecclesia pro Christo mori non dubitaret
headnotes.en: …ut spot, thou art chaste within and without. For great is the friendship between Christ and the Church, since both Christ would not hesitate to die for the [sic: *Ecelesia*], and the Church for Christ

headnotes.la: Vox Ecclesiae
headnotes.en: The voice of the Church

headnotes.la: Oculi, inquit, tui, memoria, et intellectus, et ratio columbarum sunt, id est casti et simplices. Nullatenus enim de intellectu vel sapientiae superbis. Tu enim ex illis non es, qui dicunt
headnotes.en: … he says — thy memory, thy understanding, and thy reason — are those of doves, that is, chaste and simple. For in no way art thou proud of understanding or of wisdom. For thou art not of those who say

headnotes.la: Vox Ecclesiae, vel Christi
headnotes.en: The voice of the Church, or of Christ

headnotes.la: In hoc enim maxima utriusque concordia comprobatur, quod utique utrumque de pulchritudine laudat. Hujus decor et pulchritudo nec dici quidem, nec cogitari potest
headnotes.en: For in this the greatest concord of them both is proved, that each of the two indeed praises the other for beauty. His comeliness and beauty can neither be spoken nor even conceived

headnotes.la: Quid per lectulum, nisi cor? Unde ipse Dominus ait
headnotes.en: What is meant by the little bed, if not the heart? Whence the Lord himself says

headnotes.la: …idus est, virtutibus et conscientiae puritate. Possumus autem et per hunc lectulum illam sanctorum beatitudinem intelligere, in qua in perpetua quiete, et otio quiescentes, sicut palma justi florebunt
headnotes.en: …and with purity of conscience. And we may understand by this little bed also that blessedness of the saints, in which, resting in perpetual quiet and repose, the just shall flourish like the palm tree

headnotes.la: Vox Christi
headnotes.en: The voice of Christ

headnotes.la: …rum esse, et decorum negat, quin imo totius mundi florem, et pulchritudinem, et honorem esse confirmat. Est praeterea flos campi, id est illius virginis, et inaratae terrae filius, de qua scriptum est
headnotes.en: … rather affirms that he is the flower and the beauty and the honor of the whole world. He is moreover the flower of the field, that is, the son of that virgin and unplowed earth of which it is written

headnotes.la: Unde Isaias
headnotes.en: Whence Isaias

headnotes.la: Hoc enim lilium non montium, sed convallium est; quoniam non superbos, sed humiles Dominus diligit. Sicut ipse ait
headnotes.en: For this lily is not of the mountains but of the valleys, since the Lord loves not the proud but the humble. As he himself says

headnotes.la: In convalle nascitur lilium, in humilium corde habitat Salvator
headnotes.en: The lily is born in the valley; the Savior dwells in the heart of the humble

headnotes.la: … a Judaeis autem affligitur, vulneratur et crucifigitur Christus. Inter spinas lilium crescit, quoniam a ligno Christus regnat. Hoc autem lilium in cruce suavissimum Patri dedit odorem. Unde Psalmista
headnotes.en: …hrist is afflicted, wounded, and crucified. Among thorns the lily grows, since Christ reigns from the tree. And this lily upon the cross gave forth a most sweet odor to the Father. Whence the Psalmist

headnotes.la: Vox Ecclesiae
headnotes.en: The voice of the Church

headnotes.la: Sicut enim malum inter ligna infructuosa fructuosum est; ita et Christus inter Judaeos, aliquando et apostolos fuit. Hoc est enim illud lignum, de quo dicitur quod
headnotes.en: For as the apple tree is fruitful among unfruitful trees, so was Christ among the Jews, and once among the apostles too. For this is that tree of which it is said that

headnotes.la: Erant enim tunc temporis apostoli sine fructu, cum multos in Judaea Christus daret fructus. Ad ejus autem comparationem non solum sine fructu, verum etiam sicci videbantur. Unde ipse ait
headnotes.en: For at that time the apostles were without fruit, while Christ was yielding many fruits in Judaea. And in comparison with him they seemed not only without fruit, but even dry. Whence he himself says

headnotes.la: … XXIII, 31.)] Hi autem qui prius aridi et infructuosi erant, hujus ligni pomis degustatis, sanctoque Spiritu accepto, quanta fertilitate fructificarent, ab ipsius Salvatoris verbis percipitur, qui ait
headnotes.en: …ertility these men, who before were dry and unfruitful, would bear once they had tasted the apples of this tree and received the Holy Spirit, is gathered from the words of the Savior himself, who says

headnotes.la: Sub umbra, inquit, sedi, de fructibus arboris hujus cognovi, ejusque in contemplatione sum refecta, dulcibus et eloquiis satiata. De his enim fructibus, et alibi Ecclesia dicit
headnotes.en: …shadow, she says, I sat down, I came to know the fruits of this tree, and I was refreshed in the contemplation of him, and filled with sweet sayings. For of these fruits the Church says also elsewhere

headnotes.la: Quid per cellam vinariam, nisi Novi Veterisque Testamenti doctrina? De hac enim cella dicitur
headnotes.en: What is meant by the wine cellar, if not the teaching of the New and Old Testament? For of this cellar it is said

headnotes.la: De hujus namque cellae vino Apostolus ebrius dicebat
headnotes.en: For drunk with the wine of this cellar the Apostle said

headnotes.la: Et Psalmista
headnotes.en: And the Psalmist

headnotes.la: [n: (Psal. XXII, 5.)] Hanc autem in cellam Ecclesia introducta, superni vini dulcedine inebriatur
headnotes.en: [n: (Psal. XXII, 5.)] And the Church, brought into this cellar, is made drunk with the sweetness of the wine from on high

headnotes.la: Quomodo in hac cella charitas ordinatur? Vis audire?
headnotes.en: How is charity set in order in this cellar? Wilt thou hear?

headnotes.la: Quid ultra?
headnotes.en: What further?

headnotes.la: Hic est ordo, et vera regula charitatis, ut et Deum super omnia, et proximum sicut nos ipsos, diligamus. Ordinavit in prima cella; ordinavit et in secunda. In prima autem *611* quomodo?
headnotes.en: … true rule of charity, that we love both God above all things, and our neighbor as ourselves. He set it in order in the first cellar; he set it in order in the second also. And in the first *611* how?

headnotes.la: Quid dicitur in secunda?
headnotes.en: What is said in the second?

headnotes.la: …veniens; alioquin ordo non esset. Quod enim in primo de vitio, in secundo de natura intelligitur, ut sic dicatur: inimicum odio habebis; vitium, non naturam. Diliges inimicum tuum, naturam, non vitium
headnotes.en: … first is understood of vice, in the second is understood of nature, so that it is said thus: Thou shalt hate thy enemy — the vice, not the nature. Thou shalt love thy enemy — the nature, not the vice

headnotes.la: …ala, credentes intelligimus. Possumus etiam per flores operis initium, per mala vero perfectionem intelligere. Flores enim poma fiunt, cum auditores sententiis credunt, et quae credunt, opere complent
headnotes.en: …ay also understand by the flowers the beginning of a work, and by the apples its perfection. For the flowers become fruits when the hearers believe the sentences, and fulfill in deed what they believe

headnotes.la: …llam introduxit, et vinum bibere jussit. Dedit mihi charitatem, virtutum omnium matrem. Laeva caput sublevatur, dextera caput amplexatur. Ad hoc nisi me amaret, quis pro eo me adjuraret? Vox Ecclesiae
headnotes.en: …e mother of all the virtues. By his left hand the head is lifted up, by his right hand the head is embraced. Besides this, unless he loved me, who would adjure me for his sake? The voice of the Church

headnotes.la: Sed quomodo veniet?
headnotes.en: But how shall he come?

headnotes.la: …quos Christus saliens habitavit. Sed si tu, o homo, mons fieri cupis, erige mentem, ut a terrenis cupiditatibus *612* spes, et cor tuum exaltetur. Mox enim in te saliet, qui in montibus salire dicitur
headnotes.en: …u, O man, desirest to become a mountain, lift up thy mind, that from earthly desires thy hope *612* and thy heart may be exalted. For soon he will leap into thee who is said to leap upon the mountains

headnotes.la: Vere utique colles transiliens, quoniam et sanctos sanctitate, et potentes omnes potentia transcendit
headnotes.en: Truly indeed skipping over the hills, since he surpasses both the saints in sanctity and all the mighty in power

headnotes.la: [n: (Psal. LXXXVIII.)] --
headnotes.en: [n: (Psal. LXXXVIII.)] --

headnotes.la: Quid vero per parietem, nisi peccatum? Hoc enim interposito, Deo conjungi non possumus. Noster autem dicitur paries, quoniam nos ipsi eum fabricavimus. De hoc autem, et per Psalmistam dicitur
headnotes.en: …hat is meant by the wall, if not sin? For when this is set between, we cannot be joined to God. And it is called our wall, since we ourselves built it. And of this it is said also through the Psalmist

headnotes.la: …t per cancellos, quoniam nullus in choro cantat, cujus non videat voluntatem. Videt monachum, videt episcopum, videt qui ore, qui corde psallat. Cognoscit enim qui pro amore, vel qui pro favore cantat
headnotes.en: …e no one sings in the choir whose will he does not see. He sees the monk, he sees the bishop, he sees who sings with the mouth and who with the heart. For he knows who sings for love and who for favor

headnotes.la: Unde Isaias
headnotes.en: Whence Isaias

headnotes.la: inquit. Surgite apostoli, praedicate doctores, nuntiate Evangelium. Columba mea sine felle, absque amaritudine, innocens et simplex. Unde ipse ait
headnotes.en: he says. Arise, ye apostles; preach, ye doctors; announce the Gospel. My dove, without gall, without bitterness, innocent and simple. Whence he himself says

headnotes.la: Formosa mea super nivem dealbata, sine macula et ruga. Surge, inquit, fac quod factura es, et ad me tandem post malitiam, et peracto officio veni
headnotes.en: My comely one, made whiter than snow, without spot or wrinkle. Arise, he says, do what thou art to do, and come to me at last, after the malice, and when thine office is fulfilled

headnotes.la: Transiit, inquit, hiems et imber, transiit tempus nebulosum, asperum et grave
headnotes.en: The winter and the rain are past, he says; the cloudy, harsh, and heavy season is past

headnotes.la: omnia jam clara, omnia jam nuda et manifesta sunt
headnotes.en: all things are now bright, all things now bare and manifest

headnotes.la: Hoc autem est, quod Dominus in Evangelio discipulis ait
headnotes.en: And this is what the Lord says in the Gospel to his disciples

headnotes.la: Nunc tempus metendi, nunc tempus in unam fidem gentes colligendi, tempus est vitia resecandi. Amputate vineas, ut oriantur uvae; amputate vitia, ut oriantur virtutes
headnotes.en: … the time of reaping, now the time of gathering the nations into one faith; it is the time of cutting away vices. Prune the vines, that grapes may spring up; cut away vices, that virtues may spring up

headnotes.la: Vox, inquit, turturis vox casta, vox apostolica audita est in terra nostra
headnotes.en: The voice of the turtledove, he says — the chaste voice, the apostolic voice — is heard in our land

headnotes.la: Quid per ficum nisi Synagoga? Haec autem protulit grossos suos; dedit primitias ficus, patriarchas videlicet et prophetas
headnotes.en: What is meant by the fig tree, if not the Synagogue? And she has put forth her green figs; she has given the first fruits of the fig, namely the patriarchs and the prophets

headnotes.la: Ne dormias, inquit, sed surge, et per fidem et dilectionem bonum operare
headnotes.en: Sleep not, he says, but arise, and work good through faith and love

headnotes.la: cui tantae dilectionis amore conjunctus sum, ut tuam pro te carnem sumere dignarer
headnotes.en: to whom I am joined with the love of so great an affection that I deigned to take thy flesh for thee

headnotes.la: Columba, inquit, mea, felle, omnique amaritudine carens, veni post me, sequere me, ducem non habeas nisi me
headnotes.en: My dove, he says, lacking gall and all bitterness, come after me, follow me, have no leader but me

headnotes.la: …meae carnis vulneribus delectare; tuaeque salutis haec vulnera fuisse causam agnoscas. Moram *613* namque fecerat Thomas, nec credere volebat; qui postea in hujus lapidis vulneribus delectatus, inquit
headnotes.en: … wounds of my flesh, and acknowledge that these wounds were the cause of thy salvation. For Thomas had delayed *613* and would not believe, who afterwards, delighting in the wounds of this stone, said

headnotes.la: …us etiam per maceriae cavernam, doctorum et angelorum custodiam intelligere, ut nunc quasi infra macerias posita eorum munimine tueatur; quae prius palam, et sine munitione vitiorum impetu quatiebatur
headnotes.en: …octors and of the angels, so that now, set as it were within enclosure walls, she may be protected by their defense — she who before was shaken openly and without fortification by the assault of vices

headnotes.la: Probetur qualis sit innovatio, et pulchritudo tua, doce alios ut te; nullum timeas praeter me
headnotes.en: Let it be proved of what sort thy renewal and thy beauty are; teach others as thyself; fear no one but me

headnotes.la: Me, inquit, praedica et confitere, ut a te et ab aliis per te laus mihi, et honor debitus reddatur
headnotes.en: Preach me, he says, and confess me, that by thee and by others through thee the praise and honor due to me may be rendered

headnotes.la: Quam audire volo,
headnotes.en: which I wish to hear,

headnotes.la: quam videre cupio. Praeparet se sponsa, et vestibus ornet, quae a tanto talique sponso est conspicienda. Loquatur non fictitia, vel inhonesta, imo dulcia et suavia verba. Vox adversus haereses
headnotes.en: … adorn herself with garments, she who is to be looked upon by so great and such a bridegroom. Let her speak words not feigned or dishonorable, but rather sweet and pleasant. The voice against heresies

headnotes.la: Quid per vulpes, nisi haereticos, vitia et malignos spiritus? Haec autem dum parva sunt, et in ipso suae originis principio capienda, tenenda et destruenda sunt. Unde Psalmista
headnotes.en: … by the foxes, if not heretics, vices, and malignant spirits? And these, while they are small and in the very beginning of their origin, are to be caught, held fast, and destroyed. Whence the Psalmist

headnotes.la: Nam vinea
headnotes.en: For the vine

headnotes.la: Vox Ecclesiae sic
headnotes.en: The voice of the Church thus

headnotes.la: Dilectus, inquit, meus mihi auxilium praestat, et virtutem. Ego autem illi servio, et per omnia obedio
headnotes.en: My beloved, she says, furnishes me help and strength. And I serve him, and in all things obey him

headnotes.la: Unde ipse ait
headnotes.en: Whence he himself says

headnotes.la: Dies enim tunc aspirabit, quando sol justitiae orietur sanctis, et illa incipiet, quae nunquam finem habebit. De qua dicitur
headnotes.en: For the day will then breathe when the sun of justice shall rise upon the saints, and that day will begin which shall never have an end. Of which it is said

headnotes.la: Umbrae vero inclinabuntur; quia vitae hujus cessantibus adversis, cum satellitibus suis tenebrarum princeps in infernum praecipitabitur
headnotes.en: And the shadows shall decline, because, when the adversities of this life cease, the prince of darkness with his satellites shall be cast headlong into hell

headnotes.la: Coelos, inquit, ascendisti, praelioque peracto ad Patrem rediisti. Sed revertere inspice terras, tuorumque preces exaudi
headnotes.en: Thou hast ascended, she says, into the heavens, and, the battle being finished, thou hast returned to the Father. But return, look upon the earth, and hear the prayers of thine own

headnotes.la: quae super montes appetit,
headnotes.en: which makes for the mountains,

headnotes.la: …milis igitur est capreae coelos ascendens; hinnulo vero matrem revisitans in sanctis, qui vitiorum aestu minime exuruntur; habitans, atque iterum in secundo adventu Judaeorum sese oculis repraesentans
headnotes.en: …the heavens; but like the fawn revisiting its mother, dwelling in the saints, who are in no way scorched by the heat of vices, and again presenting himself in his second coming to the eyes of the Jews

headnotes.la: Vox Ecclesiae
headnotes.en: The voice of the Church

headnotes.la: …n humana sapientia, mentis caecitate. Ideoque non inveni. Hoc enim haeretici, hoc philosophi quaesierunt; sed in nocte quaerentes suaque in sapientia confidentes, non invenerunt. Unde ipse Dominus ait
headnotes.en: …ness of mind. And therefore I found him not. For this the heretics, this the philosophers sought; but seeking by night and trusting in their own wisdom they found him not. Whence the Lord himself says

headnotes.la: Surgam, inquit Ecclesia. Sed quae Ecclesia? Ecclesia gentium, populus qui sedebat in tenebris, somnoque deditus, qui nondum dixerat
headnotes.en: I will rise, says the Church. But what Church? The Church of the Gentiles, the people that sat in darkness and was given over to sleep, which had not yet said

headnotes.la: Surgam, inquit, non amplius dormiam, *614* circuibo civitatem, id est sanctorum, apostolorumque congregationem; ut me de Deo ea doceant quae per me scire nequivi
headnotes.en: …, I will sleep no more; *614* I will go about the city, that is, the congregation of the saints and of the apostles, that they may teach me concerning God those things which I could not know by myself

headnotes.la: Hoc autem per noctem, hoc in lectulo meo. Quaeram igitur in die, quatenus eum inveniam
headnotes.en: But this was by night, this in my little bed. I will seek him therefore by day, that I may find him

headnotes.la: …inveniunt, qui Deum fide et baptismate quaerunt. In hoc enim custodum cura circumdatur, quae non ipsa eos. verum etiam ipsi eam invenisse dicuntur. His autem inventis, dixi (Ecclesia de Christo dicit)
headnotes.en: …aith and by baptism. For in this the care of the guardians is set about her, who not she them. but they also are said to have found her. And when these were found, I said (the Church speaks of Christ)

headnotes.la: Hoc autem tale est ac si diceret: Vos qui Dei cognitionem habetis, Deum ipsum, veritatisque viam mihi monstrate
headnotes.en: And this is as if she should say: You who have the knowledge of God, show me God himself and the way of truth

headnotes.la: …telligendo eos pertransissem, cumque eorum monita et praedicationem transcurrerem (hoc enim locutionis modo, transcurro librum, dicere solemus), inveni per eorum demonstrationem quem diligit anima mea
headnotes.en: …passed by them, and when I ran through their admonitions and their preaching (for by this manner of speech we are wont to say, I run through a book), I found, by their showing, him whom my soul loveth

headnotes.la: Inveni, inquit, et dulciter eum amplexata sum
headnotes.en: I found him, she says, and sweetly embraced him

headnotes.la: Quomodo? mente, et operatione, et fide perfecta
headnotes.en: How? In mind, and in work, and in perfect faith

headnotes.la: sed ardentissimo amore ei inhaerebo
headnotes.en: but with most burning love I will cleave to him

headnotes.la: id est in hujus fictilis vasis habitaculum, quod ipse manibus suis, genitrice terra, plasmavit. Sancti enim Dei sunt habitaculum. Unde ipse ait
headnotes.en: that is, into the dwelling of this earthen vessel, which he himself formed with his own hands, the earth being its parent. For the saints are the dwelling of God. Whence he himself says

headnotes.la: Id est in secretarium cordis mei. Possumus autem et per hanc matrem Synagogam intelligere, a cujus domo Christus exivit, ex quo dixit
headnotes.en: That is, into the secret place of my heart. And we may understand by this mother also the Synagogue, from whose house Christ went out, from the time when he said

headnotes.la: tunc in suae genitricis domum Ecclesiam introducet
headnotes.en: then will he bring the Church into the house of her that bore her

headnotes.la: Sponsus ad fideles animas
headnotes.en: The Bridegroom to faithful souls

headnotes.la: …re magnum est peccatum. Diversae namque sunt gratiae, diversae sunt voluntates, diversae sunt et operationes quibus Domino servire possumus. Unusquisque ergo in suo sensu abundet. Synagoga de Ecclesia
headnotes.en: …in. For the graces are diverse, the wills are diverse, and diverse too are the works by which we can serve the Lord. Let each one therefore abound in his own sense. The Synagogue concerning the Church

headnotes.la: …t per hujus saeculi adversa, non latronum insidias, non tyrannorum gladios, non leonum dentes, non Judaeorum et haereticorum sophismata timens, ad Dominum Ecclesia pertransivit. Sed quomodo transivit?
headnotes.en: …s of this world the Church passed over to the Lord, fearing not the ambushes of robbers, nor the swords of tyrants, nor the teeth of lions, nor the sophisms of Jews and heretics. But how did she pass?

headnotes.la: Vox Ecclesiae
headnotes.en: The voice of the Church

headnotes.la: Salomon namque *pacificus* interpretatur
headnotes.en: For Solomon is interpreted *peaceable*

headnotes.la: Lectulum igitur Salomonis *615* Ecclesiam intelligimus, quam sibi pio amore Christus sociavit, non habentem maculam neque rugam. De qua per Prophetam ait
headnotes.en: By the little bed of Solomon, therefore, we understand *615* the Church, whom Christ has joined to himself with devoted love, not having spot or wrinkle. Of whom he says through the Prophet

headnotes.la: …i, et legis documentis, et institutionibus sapientes esse debent. Hi autem non solum fortes, verum etiam ex fortissimis Israel esse dicuntur, quoniam Ecclesiae doctores caeteris fortiores esse oportet
headnotes.en: …orks and wise in the teachings and institutions of the law. And these are said to be not only valiant, but of the most valiant of Israel, since the doctors of the Church must be stronger than the rest

headnotes.la: Unde et Psalmista
headnotes.en: Whence also the Psalmist

headnotes.la: Et Apostolus
headnotes.en: And the Apostle

headnotes.la: Teneant igitur episcopi gladios, quibus et vitia destruant, et Ecclesiam defendant
headnotes.en: Let the bishops therefore hold swords, with which they may both destroy vices and defend the Church

headnotes.la: Unde est illud
headnotes.en: Whence is that saying

headnotes.la: Doctissimi namque in praelio sunt, quoniam patiendo, non se ipsos defendendo, in humilitate et patientia vicerunt
headnotes.en: For they are most expert in battle, since by suffering, not by defending themselves, they conquered in humility and patience

headnotes.la: Super femur namque enses habent, qui impetus libidinis castitatis freno repellunt. Unde Apostolus
headnotes.en: For they have swords upon their thigh who drive back the assaults of lust with the bridle of chastity. Whence the Apostle

headnotes.la: Armati, inquit, sunt doctores, et gladiis accincti, ne haeretici et maligni spiritus in nocte dolo et occulte Salomonis lectum invadant, id est sanctam Ecclesiam. Ecclesia
headnotes.en: The doctors, he says, are armed and girt with swords, lest the heretics and the malignant spirits should by night, by guile and in secret, invade the bed of Solomon, that is, holy Church. The Church

headnotes.la: …onis domum de lignis Libani fecit Dominus, quoniam nullus in Ecclesia habitat, qui baptismatis aqua non sit candidatus. Libanus enim *candidatio* interpretatur. De hoc autem ferculo in Psalmis dicitur
headnotes.en: … of the woods of Libanus, since no one dwells in the Church who has not been made white by the water of baptism. For Libanus is interpreted *whitening*. And of this *ferculum* it is said in the Psalms

headnotes.la: … manducandum Christus apposuit. Hic panem vivum, hic agnum praefiguratum, taurumque saginatum comedimus, hic calicem Novi Testamenti potamus, hic divino et dulcissimo vino inebriamur. De Christo dicit
headnotes.en: …re we eat the living bread, here the prefigured lamb and the fatted bull; here we drink the chalice of the New Testament, here we are made drunk with the divine and most sweet wine. She says of Christ

headnotes.la: Quid per columnas nisi apostolos et doctores; sed quare columnae, nisi quia totius Ecclesiae sunt sustentamenta? De his in Psalmis dicitur
headnotes.en: What is meant by the pillars, if not the apostles and the doctors? And why pillars, if not because they are the supports of the whole Church? Of these it is said in the Psalms

headnotes.la: Cur autem argenteae, nisi quia simplicitatis, modestiae, et sobrietatis affectione pallent? Hi sunt illae pennae columnae, quae deargentatae esse dicuntur
headnotes.en: And why of silver, if not because they are pale with the affection of simplicity, modesty, and sobriety? These are those feathers of the pillar which are said to be silvered over

headnotes.la: Mensam, inquit, et reclinatorium aureum fecit, quoniam Novum et Vetus Testamentum sapientiae luce praefulgent. De hac autem mensa dicitur
headnotes.en: He made, she says, a table and a resting-place of gold, since the New and the Old Testament shine forth with the light of wisdom. And of this table it is said

headnotes.la: Accedamus igitur ad hanc auream mensam, ut divinis et spiritualibus dapibus reficiamur
headnotes.en: Let us draw near, therefore, to this golden table, that we may be refreshed with divine and spiritual feasts

headnotes.la: Accedamus igitur ad hanc auream mensam, ut divinis et spiritualibus dapibus reficiamur. « Ascensum purpureum
headnotes.en: Let us draw near, therefore, to this golden table, that we may be refreshed with divine and spiritual feasts. « An ascent of purple

headnotes.la: …iamur. « Ascensum purpureum. « Nullus enim hujus mensae cibos comedit, nisi per purpuream viam ascendat. Non enim Judaei hujus cibum capiunt, quoniam ascensum purpureum non noverunt. De quibus dicitur
headnotes.en: …An ascent of purple. « For no one eats the food of this table unless he ascend by the purple way. For the Jews do not take this food, since they have not known the ascent of purple. Of whom it is said

headnotes.la: …er animas simplices, quae in infernales tenebras mergebantur. Constravit et media charitate, quia pro universali salute crucifixus, salutem in medio terrae operatus est. Vox Ecclesiae de Christo dicit
headnotes.en: …rkness of hell. And he paved it with charity in the midst, because, crucified for the salvation of all, he wrought salvation in the midst of the earth. The voice of the Church speaks concerning Christ

headnotes.la: Egredimini, inquit, filiae Sion, extra portam; exite, filiae Jerusalem, et videte regem vestrum, videte Salomonem, videte Christum vere pacificum
headnotes.en: Go forth, she says, ye daughters of Sion, outside the gate; come out, ye daughters of Jerusalem, and see your King, see Solomon, see Christ the truly peaceable

headnotes.la: …nagoga intelligitur, quoniam ex Judaica *616* gente secundum carnem natus est Dominus. Haec autem filium suum, dominum suum, regem suum coronavit, spineamque coronam super caput ejus imposuit. Quando?
headnotes.en: …s understood to be the Synagogue, since according to the flesh the Lord was born of the Jewish *616* nation. And she crowned her son, her lord, her king, and set a crown of thorns upon his head. When?

headnotes.la: …sponsavit, ipsiusque de latere dormientis conjugem fabricavit. Namque sicut de dormiente Adam, una costa subtracta, facta est Eva, ita de Christo dormiente, latere lancea perforato, facta est Ecclesia
headnotes.en: …and from the side of him as he slept fashioned a spouse. For as from Adam sleeping, one rib being drawn out, Eve was made, so from Christ sleeping, his side pierced with the lance, the Church was made

headnotes.la: Vox Christi
headnotes.en: The voice of Christ

headnotes.la: Cur autem bis dixit quam pulchra es, nisi quia in opere et sermone, interius et exterius, in anima et corpore pulchra est?
headnotes.en: And why did he say twice, how beautiful art thou, if not because she is beautiful in work and in speech, within and without, in soul and in body?

headnotes.la: id est intellectus, ratio, intuitus tuus simplex est et acutus, non ira confusus, non furoris sanguine perturbatus, non in superbiam elatus
headnotes.en: that is, thy understanding, thy reason, thy gaze is simple and keen, not confounded by anger, not disturbed by the blood of rage, not lifted up into pride

headnotes.la: … maxima spes. Possumus etiam et per oculos prophetas intelligere, qui ea quae futura erant multo ante praeviderant. Hi columbae dicuntur, quoniam in humilitate et simplicitate cordis Domino servierunt
headnotes.en: … hope. We may also understand by the eyes the prophets, who long beforehand foresaw the things that were to come. These are called doves, since they served the Lord in humility and simplicity of heart

headnotes.la: …; siquidem secundum tempus totius Ecclesiae sunt superiores. Sed quare gregi caprarum assimilantur, nisi quia carnaliter vivebant, et luxuriae carnisque voluptatibus serviebant? His enim dictum fuerat
headnotes.en: … they are higher than the whole Church. But why are they likened to a flock of goats, if not because they lived carnally, and served luxury and the pleasures of the flesh? For to them it had been said

headnotes.la: Ex talibus autem David et Salomon fuisse probantur, quorum concubinarum non erat numerus. Sola igitur fide isti salvantur. Hi sunt, qui per fidem vicerunt regna
headnotes.en: And of such sort David and Solomon are proved to have been, of whose concubines there was no number. By faith alone therefore are these saved. These are they who by faith conquered kingdoms

headnotes.la: Galaad namque *acervus testimonii* interpretatur. Ascenderunt igitur de monte Galaad, quia legis et prophetarum testimonia observantes coelorum regna scandere meruerunt
headnotes.en: … Galaad is interpreted *a heap of testimony*. They came up therefore from mount Galaad, because, observing the testimonies of the law and of the prophets, they deserved to climb the kingdoms of heaven

headnotes.la: …pascunt et nutriunt? Cur autem greges tonsarum ovium, nisi quia saecularibus omnibus venditis, et pauperibus attributis, nudi, tonsi, vitiis exspoliati in innocentia et simplicitate Domino servierunt?
headnotes.en: …urch? And why flocks of shorn sheep, if not because, when all worldly things had been sold and given to the poor, they served the Lord naked, shorn, and stripped of vices, in innocence and simplicity?

headnotes.la: De lavacro quidem ascenderunt, quoniam baptismatis aqua mundati, vitiisque omnibus expulsis, ad summum fidei et doctrinae, et ad coelos sublimati sunt
headnotes.en: From the washing indeed they came up, since, cleansed by the water of baptism and with all vices driven out, they were raised to the summit of faith and doctrine, and to the heavens

headnotes.la: …eros dormientes Novum et Vetus praedicant Testamentum. Possumus autem et per gemellos fetus doctrinam et operationem intelligere, sive etiam carnis et animae castitatem, vel Dei et proximi dilectionem
headnotes.en: …st of the lots, they preach the New and the Old Testament. And we may understand by the twin young also teaching and work, or else the chastity of flesh and of soul, or the love of God and of neighbor

headnotes.la: …tationes comprimunt, ne vento vanitatis per inania rapiantur. Cur autem coccineae? Quia et igne sancti Spiritus accensi sunt, et Christi praedicant passionem. Coccus ignis, vel sanguinis speciem habet
headnotes.en: …h empty things by the wind of vanity. And why scarlet? Because they are both kindled with the fire of the Holy Spirit, and preach the passion of Christ. Scarlet has the appearance of fire, or of blood

headnotes.la: Dulcia quidem sunt sanctorum eloquia, et auditu suavia. Unde et illud
headnotes.en: Sweet indeed are the sayings of the saints, and pleasant to hear. Whence also that word

headnotes.la: [n: (Psal. CXVIII, 103)] --
headnotes.en: [n: (Psal. CXVIII, 103)] --

headnotes.la: …oprio sanguine cruentati sunt. Genae igitur dicuntur, quia et de peccatis erubescunt; fragmen autem, quoniam pro Christi nomine trucidantur et franguntur; mali vero punici propter sanguinis effusionem
headnotes.en: …d. They are called cheeks, then, because they also blush for their sins; a piece, because they are slaughtered and broken for the name of Christ; and of a pomegranate, because of the shedding of blood

headnotes.la: Pulchrae, inquit, sunt genae, rosea est facies, virginalis et pudicus est vultus; multo tamen laudabiliora sunt, quae nondum apparent, quae in corde latent, quae in coelesti thesauro tibi reservantur
headnotes.en: …rosy is thy face, virginal and chaste is thy countenance; yet far more praiseworthy are the things which do not yet appear, which lie hid in the heart, which are kept for thee in the heavenly treasury

headnotes.la: Sic autem et doctores propugnacula habent, sapientiam videlicet et virtutem, quae nulla possunt machina expugnari, nullisque inimicorum instrumentis destrui
headnotes.en: And so the doctors too have bulwarks, namely wisdom and virtue, which can be stormed by no engine, nor destroyed by any instruments of the enemy

headnotes.la: Mille namque clypei pendent a doctoribus, quoniam per innumerabiles sententias et argumentationes ab eis defluentes, Ecclesiam protegunt
headnotes.en: For a thousand shields hang from the doctors, since by innumerable sentences and arguments flowing down from them they protect the Church

headnotes.la: Nihil enim in ea vinci, vel frangi potest
headnotes.en: For nothing in her can be conquered or broken

headnotes.la: …melli. Duo namque ubera duo Testamenta sunt. Duo vero gemelli duos populos designant: Judaicum videlicet et gentilem. Hi autem gemelli dicuntur, quoniam et gemini sunt, et geminam charitatem observant
headnotes.en: …two breasts are the two Testaments. And the two twins designate two peoples, namely the Jewish and the Gentile. And these are called twins, since they are both born together and keep a twofold charity

headnotes.la: In liliis quidem pascuntur, qui in suavibus et odoriferis Scripturarum sententiis delectantur
headnotes.en: They feed indeed among the lilies who take delight in the sweet and fragrant sentences of the Scriptures

headnotes.la: illa scilicet de qua dicitur: Quia
headnotes.en: that day, namely, of which it is said: For

headnotes.la: fugiatque caligo, et tenebrarum omnium princeps cum tota militia sua in infernum praecipitetur. Sponsus de sponsa dicit
headnotes.en: and let the gloom flee, and let the prince of all darkness with his whole army be cast headlong into hell. The Bridegroom says concerning the bride

headnotes.la: …nem suscipiam. Mons namque myrrhae caro est, quam assumpsit. Hic autem est ille mons, qui tantum crevit, ut totam terram compleret. Myrrhae autem ideo dicitur, quia corruptionem non vidit; juxta illud
headnotes.en: …h is the flesh which he took. And this is that mountain which grew so great that it filled the whole earth. And it is called of myrrh for this reason, that it saw no corruption; according to that word

headnotes.la: id est ad eos, quorum orationes me oblectant, sicut suavis odor thuris
headnotes.en: that is, to those whose prayers delight me as the sweet odor of frankincense

headnotes.la: Tota namque pulchra est, quia neque maculam, neque rugam habet. Sponsus ad sponsam
headnotes.en: For she is all beautiful, because she has neither spot nor wrinkle. The Bridegroom to the bride

headnotes.la: …te nites; nihil tenebrosum, nihil nigrum, nihil obscurum in te esse conspicitur. Veni igitur ad me, et quae semper pulchritudinem dilexisti, sicut sol in regno meo fulgeas in aeternum. Ter autem dixit
headnotes.en: …tity of flowers; nothing dark, nothing black, nothing obscure is seen to be in thee. Come therefore to me, and thou who hast always loved beauty, shine like the sun in my kingdom for ever. And he said

headnotes.la: quia tria sunt, sine quibus non ad eum venitur; id est fides, spes, et charitas; *618* sive quia cogitatione, locutione, operatione Domino servit. Cur autem sponsa vocetur, superius dictum est
headnotes.en: …ithout which one does not come to him — that is, faith, hope, and charity; *618* or else because she serves the Lord in thought, in speech, and in work. And why she is called bride has been said above

headnotes.la: Hi autem montes in Judaea sunt. In his autem leones et pardi habitant, sicut sequentia manifestant
headnotes.en: And these mountains are in Judaea. And in them lions and leopards dwell, as what follows makes plain

headnotes.la: Per hos autem montes, illos intelligimus, in quibus vitiorum exercitus, leones, et pardi, et ipsi maligni spiritus inhabitant. His autem devictis et expulsis, coronatur Ecclesia
headnotes.en: …by these mountains we understand those men in whom the army of vices, lions and leopards, and the malignant spirits themselves, dwell. And when these are overcome and driven out, the Church is crowned

headnotes.la: Coronatur igitur de supradictorum montium capite, quia diabolo devicto, qui illorum caput et dominus est, pro tanto certamine praemium suscipit, et coronam
headnotes.en: She is crowned, therefore, from the head of the aforesaid mountains, because, the devil being overcome, who is their head and lord, she receives the prize and the crown for so great a struggle

headnotes.la: Soror quidem, quia ejusdem patris filia est. Unde Apostolus ait
headnotes.en: Sister indeed, because she is the daughter of the same Father. Whence the Apostle says

headnotes.la: Sponsa vero, quia carnem nostram sumens de virginali utero Christus processit. Haec autem soror et conjux sponsi sui cor vulneravit, amore scilicet, mortisque timore
headnotes.en: And spouse, because, taking our flesh, Christ came forth from a virginal womb. And this sister and wife wounded the heart of her bridegroom, namely with love and with the fear of death

headnotes.la: …insidias; unum tantum oculum splendidissimum habet; una Trinitatis fide illuminatur, sine qua Deo nullus placebit. Hunc autem oculum qui non habent, caeci sunt, et in tenebris ambulant. Unde Apostolus
headnotes.en: …eye that is most shining; she is enlightened by the one faith of the Trinity, without which no one shall please God. And those who have not this eye are blind, and walk in darkness. Whence the Apostle

headnotes.la: …utem crinis, una est sententia, quae apud omnes eadem est, in qua Christianorum nullus dissidet, quam apostoli praedicaverunt, et pro qua martyres sanguinem fuderunt, quam sancti Patres confirmaverunt
headnotes.en: …d the one hair is the one sentence which is the same among all, in which no Christian differs, which the apostles preached, and for which the martyrs shed their blood, which the holy Fathers confirmed

headnotes.la: …idius et suavius est. Natos suos lactat Ecclesia, adulterinos suos inebriat Synagoga. Hi autem sapienter educati, celeriter crescunt; illi vero sicut ebrii, sensum amittunt. De quibus ipse Dominus ait
headnotes.en: …ives her own children milk; the Synagogue makes her adulterous ones drunk. And these, being wisely brought up, grow quickly; but those, like drunkards, lose their senses. Of whom the Lord himself says

headnotes.la: id est virtutum, sermonum et gratiarum. Haec enim omnia unguentum dicuntur, quia et suavia sunt, et omnium infirmitatum languores sanant
headnotes.en: that is, of thy virtues, thy discourses, and thy graces. For all these are called ointment, because they are both sweet, and heal the languors of all infirmities

headnotes.la: id est prae cunctis Judaeorum sacrificiis
headnotes.en: that is, before all the sacrifices of the Jews

headnotes.la: Favus enim mel est in cera, per quem spiritualis intelligentia significatur in littera. Favum distillant labia Ecclesiae, id est dulcia et suavia verba
headnotes.en: For a honeycomb is honey in wax, by which the spiritual understanding within the letter is signified. The lips of the Church drop a honeycomb, that is, sweet and pleasant words

headnotes.la: Quibus omne genus hominum delectatur. Possumus autem et per mel, quod de rore coeli conficitur, spiritualem et altiorem doctrinam intelligere; de qua Apostolus ait
headnotes.en: With which every kind of men is delighted. And we may also understand by honey, which is made from the dew of heaven, the spiritual and higher teaching, of which the Apostle says

headnotes.la: per lac vero mediocrem; unde ipse ait
headnotes.en: and by milk the middling teaching, whence he himself says

headnotes.la: …xuit manibus; virtutibus enim virtutes conjungens, operibusque bonis bona opera connectens, admirabilem sibi composuit vestem; in qua non minus delectatur sponsus quam in multo suavissimo thuris odore
headnotes.en: …tues to virtues, and knitting good works to good works, she has fashioned for herself a wondrous robe, in which the Bridegroom delights no less than in the abundant and most sweet odor of frankincense

headnotes.la: …ores et martyres, virgines et viduae. Conclusus autem, quoniam virtutum et angelorum munita praesidiis. Nulla vitiis patet porta, per quam latrones, et hostes subintrent, qui furentur, et rapiant bona
headnotes.en: …closed, since she is fortified with the garrisons of the virtues and of the angels. No gate lies open to vices, through which robbers and enemies might steal in, to thieve and to snatch away her goods

headnotes.la: …tis est in Ecclesia, quo et vitiorum sordes auferuntur, et animae et corporis maculae purgantur. Est autem fons vivus in horto isto, cujus aquam qui bibit, non sitiet ultra. De hoc autem fonte dicitur
headnotes.en: …ilth of vices is taken away and the stains of soul and body are cleansed. And there is a living fountain in this garden, whose water he who drinks shall thirst no more. And of this fountain it is said

headnotes.la: …r? Signatus est fons, cognoscitur aqua, ad hanc sancti currunt, hanc et vitia, et maligni spiritus fugiunt. Hoc enim signo fons iste ab aliis discernitur, quoniam quae iste fecit, alii facere nequeunt
headnotes.en: …the water is known, to it the saints run, and from it both vices and malignant spirits flee. For by this sign this fountain is distinguished from others, since what this one has done, others cannot do

headnotes.la: …quos hic hortus malorum punicorum fructus Domino mittit? Mala, inquit, punica mittit, multosque martyres Domino mandat. Mala namque punica vos estis apostoli, qui pro Christi nomine sanguinem fudistis
headnotes.en: …anates which this garden sends to the Lord? She sends pomegranates, he says, and commends many martyrs to the Lord. For the pomegranates are you, O apostles, who shed your blood for the name of Christ

headnotes.la: non solum, inquit, martyres mittit, sed cum aliorum pomorum fructibus, cum virginibus et confessoribus mala punica praesentat
headnotes.en: she sends not only martyrs, he says, but with the fruits of the other trees she presents the pomegranates together with virgins and confessors

headnotes.la: …intelligi possunt, quae et suavitate et odore omnibus praeferuntur. Cyprus namque cum nardo ponitur, quoniam qui divino et regio unguento unguntur, magnus et suavissimus odor Deo sunt. Unde Apostolus,
headnotes.en: …ll things both in sweetness and in odor. For the cyprus is set with the nard, since those who are anointed with the divine and royal ointment are a great and most sweet odor to God. Whence the Apostle

headnotes.la: …unt, nec altius crescunt, simplices et humiles intelligimus, quos, quamvis vulgo homines non venerentur, magnae tamen virtutis et sanctitatis sunt. In his autem persona est humilis, sed virtus excelsa
headnotes.en: …not grow higher, we understand the simple and the humble, who, although men commonly do not venerate them, are yet of great virtue and holiness. And in these the person is humble, but the virtue lofty

headnotes.la: …ligna Libani magnae sunt altitudinis. Myrrha vero et aloe, quae putredini, vermibusque resistunt, castitatem et alias virtutes significant, quae a vitiorum contactu et animam et corpus servant illaesa
headnotes.en: …s of Libanus are of great height. And the myrrh and the aloes, which resist rottenness and worms, signify chastity and the other virtues, which keep both soul and body unharmed from the touch of vices

headnotes.la: et maximis
headnotes.en: and greatest

headnotes.la: per quae fides, spes et charitas designari possunt, quae in saecula saeculorum detinent principatum
headnotes.en: by which faith, hope, and charity can be designated, which hold the primacy for ever and ever

headnotes.la: …qui bibunt, vivere nequeunt. Illi tamen de fonte bibunt, qui Scripturarum superficiem summis tenus labiis delibant. De puteo non sumunt profundiores aquas, id est difficiliores sententias non hauriunt
headnotes.en: …ose drink from the fountain who sip the surface of the Scriptures with the tips of their lips alone. From the well they do not take the deeper waters, that is, they do not draw up the harder sentences

headnotes.la: …constantia, virtute, et affluentia hae aquae fluunt. Sed unde fluunt? de impetu, de Libano, de monte candidato. Libanus enim, ut dictum saepe est, *candidatio* interpretatur. Christus gratias convocat
headnotes.en: … these waters flow. But whence do they flow? From the force, from Libanus, from the whitened mountain. For Libanus, as has often been said, is interpreted *whitening*. Christ calls together the graces

headnotes.la: …ectum ferebatur. Possumus tamen per aquilonem, qui asper ventus et frigidus est, tyrannorum crudelitatem intelligere. Per austrum vero, qui serenus est, fallaciae blandimenta designantur; unde dicitur
headnotes.en: …rd. Yet we may understand by the north wind, which is a harsh and cold wind, the cruelty of tyrants. And by the south wind, which is calm, the blandishments of deceit are designated; whence it is said

headnotes.la: Ecclesia de Christo dicit
headnotes.en: The Church says of Christ

headnotes.la: Veniat, inquit, dilectus meus, sponsus meus, amicus meus in hortum suum, in Ecclesiam suam, in sanctorum congregationem. Ad quid?
headnotes.en: Let him come, she says, my beloved, my Bridegroom, my friend, into his garden, into his Church, into the congregation of the saints. To what end?

headnotes.la: …sequium, et bona opera sanctorum. Mitia sunt poma, quatiuntur arbores, occiduntur martyres. Jubeat igitur Dominus, ut eorum animae in coelesti thesauro, et in sinu Abrahae congregentur. Christus dicit
headnotes.en: …saints. The apples are mellow, the trees are shaken, the martyrs are slain. Let the Lord therefore command that their souls be gathered into the heavenly treasury and into Abraham's bosom. Christ says

headnotes.la: …us, quando concupiscentiis carnis devictis, cum solis virtutibus homo conversatur. Tunc incorrupta est caro, tunc virtutes redolent, tunc ad se sanctos venire Dominus jubet. Cum enim Apostolus diceret
headnotes.en: …flesh being overcome, a man lives with the virtues alone. Then the flesh is incorrupt, then the virtues give forth their fragrance, then the Lord bids the saints come to him. For when the Apostle said

headnotes.la: nonne ut sua meteretur myrrha desiderabat?
headnotes.en: was he not longing that his own myrrh should be gathered?

headnotes.la: Quanta dulcedine et delectatione sanctos suos Deus recipiat, in his verbis declaratur
headnotes.en: With what sweetness and delight God receives his saints is declared in these words

headnotes.la: recepi amorem meum, suscepi dulcissimos, nimisque dilectos amicos meos. Confirmatio
headnotes.en: — I have received my love, I have taken up my sweetest and exceedingly beloved friends. Confirmation

headnotes.la: …cta scientia ornantur. Venit igitur Christus in hortum suum, et myrrham, quam ventus perflaverat, sanctos scilicet, quos tyrannus contristaverat, nimio secum amore devexit. Christus ad apostolos dicit
headnotes.en: …refore came into his garden, and carried away with him, with exceeding love, the myrrh which the wind had blown through — that is, the saints whom the tyrant had afflicted. Christ says to the apostles

headnotes.la: Apostropha ad apostolos. Vos, inquit, amici mei estis; vos doctrinam fidei, et carnem meam comedite, vos sanguinem meum bibite
headnotes.en: Apostrophe to the apostles. You, he says, are my friends; do you eat the doctrine of the faith and my flesh, do you drink my blood

headnotes.la: Comedite igitur panem vivum; bibite calicem novi testamenti
headnotes.en: Eat therefore the living bread; drink the cup of the new testament

headnotes.la: Qui enim hoc calice inebriatur, vera scientia inebriatur. Qui enim divitias spernit, mortem desiderat, sui obliviscitur, negligit quae videt, credit quae non videt, nonne is ebrius esse videtur?
headnotes.en: …ebriated with this cup is inebriated with true knowledge. For he who spurns riches, desires death, forgets himself, neglects what he sees, believes what he does not see — does he not seem to be drunk?

headnotes.la: …or autem vigilat, anima scilicet quae in bonis operibus perseverat. Possumus autem per cor, Christi apostolos intelligere. Isti autem vigilant, isti sanctam Ecclesiam die noctuque custodiunt. Ecclesia
headnotes.en: …e heart watches — that is, the soul, which perseveres in good works. And we may understand by the heart the apostles of Christ. These watch, these guard the holy Church by day and by night. The Church

headnotes.la: Audio, inquit, vocem Domini mei; pulsat enim sanctos suos, ne dormiant, hortatur ut vigilent. Stat enim ad ostium, et pulsat. Si quis aperuerit, intrabit, et coenabit cum illo
headnotes.en: …ays, the voice of my Lord; for he knocks at his saints, that they may not sleep, and exhorts them to watch. For he stands at the door and knocks. If any man open, he will come in and will sup with him

headnotes.la: Soror quidem, quia ejusdem patris et sponsus et sponsa, filii sunt. Ille naturaliter, ista vero adoptione
headnotes.en: Sister indeed, because both Bridegroom and bride are children of the same Father — he by nature, but she by adoption

headnotes.la: pro qua mori non dubitavi, qua major dilectio nulla est
headnotes.en: for whom I did not hesitate to die, than which love there is none greater

headnotes.la: felle, et amaritudine carens
headnotes.en: lacking gall and bitterness

headnotes.la: quae vitiis omnibus emundata sine macula es atque ruga. Aperi, inquit, mihi cor tuum, aperi mihi portam, qua et tuas, et aliorum ingrediar conscientias
headnotes.en: who, cleansed from all vices, art without spot or wrinkle. Open to me, he says, thy heart; open to me the gate by which I may enter both thy conscience and the consciences of others

headnotes.la: Confirmatio
headnotes.en: Confirmation

headnotes.la: Tota, inquit, nocte cucurri, pro tuo amore vigilavi
headnotes.en: All the night, he says, I have run; for love of thee I have kept watch

headnotes.la: Aperi mihi, soror mea. In multis quidem adversis, in nocte, et in ipsa morte pro hujus dilectione fuit Christus. Unde et illud
headnotes.en: Open to me, my sister. Christ indeed was in many adversities, in the night, and in death itself, for love of her. Whence also that word

headnotes.la: … igitur huic non aperire, et in cordis thalamum tantum sponsum non accipere. Spiritualiter autem ros in capite, et coelestis benedictio, et Spiritus sancti gratia in eo intelligitur. De quo dictum est
headnotes.en: …eat a Bridegroom into the bridal chamber of the heart. But spiritually the dew upon the head is understood both of the heavenly blessing and of the grace of the Holy Spirit in him. Of which it is said

headnotes.la: Vox fidelis animae. Sponsa ad seipsam
headnotes.en: The voice of the faithful soul. The bride to herself

headnotes.la: …nvoluta et irretita eram. Immaculata sum, et te novo homine induta, in novitate vitae ambulabo, et non amplius praedicta tunica induar, non ad saecularia revertar; sed quae incoepi, instanter operabor
headnotes.en: …hed with thee, the new man, I shall walk in newness of life, and I shall no more put on the aforesaid tunic, nor shall I return to secular things; but what I have begun I shall work at without ceasing

headnotes.la: …a terrae propior est, saepius coinquinatur. Sunt enim quaedam peccata, sine quibus vix aliquis immunis erit, Ut elatio mentis, vana gloria, verba otiosa et vanae cogitationes. Vox Ecclesiae de Christo
headnotes.en: …th, is more often defiled. For there are certain sins from which scarcely anyone will be immune, as elation of mind, vainglory, idle words, and vain thoughts. The voice of the Church concerning Christ

headnotes.la: Quis enim est, quem Dominus tetigit, sanctoque Spiritu inspiravit; quis ipsius passionem commemorans non contremiscat? Unde est illud
headnotes.en: For who is there whom the Lord has touched and inspired with the Holy Spirit — who, calling his passion to mind, would not tremble? Whence is that word

headnotes.la: Mittit igitur Dominus manum per foramen, tangit cor nostrum; recordatur passionis, stringitur admiratione et timore cum Dominus pro servis, justus pro injustis, creator pro creatura, talia pateretur
headnotes.en: …ning, he touches our heart; it remembers the passion, it is gripped with wonder and fear that the Lord should suffer such things for his servants, the just for the unjust, the creator for the creature

headnotes.la: …meae delectationis, surrexi, et saeculi blandimenta dereliqui. Aperui dilecto, credidi sermonibus, cor meum vitiis et errore mundavi, in quo tantus hospes habitaturus erat. Unde per Psalmistam dicitur
headnotes.en: … the blandishments of the world. I opened to my beloved, I believed his words, I cleansed of vices and of error my heart, in which so great a guest was to dwell. Whence it is said through the Psalmist

headnotes.la: Quid per manus nisi opera? Quid vero per myrrham, nisi incorruptionem? Distillant igitur manus myrrham, quoniam et corpus, et animam bona opera incorruptam faciunt
headnotes.en: What by the hands but works? And what by the myrrh but incorruption? The hands therefore drop myrrh, since good works make both body and soul incorrupt

headnotes.la: …vigilare, orare, jejunare, et similia. Haec autem non immerito probatissima myrrha plena esse dicuntur; quoniam et carnem non sine magna retributione mortificant, et aeternam praeparant incorruptionem
headnotes.en: …d the like. And these are not undeservedly said to be full of the most approved myrrh, since they both mortify the flesh — and that not without a great recompense — and prepare an eternal incorruption

headnotes.la: …movi, quibus quasi pessulo cor meum erat clausum. Aperui quidem, ut eum reciperem, et quis, et qualis, et quomodo sit verissime, perfecte et rationabiliter intelligerem. Sed frustra. Ut quid? Sequitur
headnotes.en: …hut as by a bolt. I opened indeed, that I might receive him, and might understand most truly, perfectly, and reasonably who he is, and of what sort, and in what manner. But in vain. Why so? It follows

headnotes.la: Cum enim ea quae Dei sunt, homines perscrutari praesumunt, ipse quidem ab eis declinat atque transit; quoniam qualiter sit, nullo modo comprehendi potest. Unde est illud
headnotes.en: For when men presume to search out the things that are God's, he indeed turns aside from them and passes on, since in what manner he is can in no way be comprehended. Whence is that word

headnotes.la: …m liquefactam tunc habemus. Judaeorum autem animae liquefactae non sunt; quoniam eorum corda nimium indurata stilo spiritus inscribi nequeunt. Quod quidem lex eorum significavit in lapidibus deformata
headnotes.en: …d. But the souls of the Jews have not melted, since their hearts, hardened beyond measure, cannot be inscribed with the stylus of the spirit. Which indeed their law signified, being shaped upon stones

headnotes.la: Quaerunt namque multi Dominum, quoniam et mundum relinquere, et de necessitatibus liberari, et cum eo esse desiderant. Unde quidam ait
headnotes.en: For many seek the Lord, since they desire both to leave the world, and to be freed from necessities, and to be with him. Whence one says

headnotes.la: [n: (Isa. LXIV, 1.)] Et Apostolus
headnotes.en: [n: (Isa. LXIV, 1.)] And the Apostle

headnotes.la: Quidam tamen quaerunt, et non statim inveniunt
headnotes.en: Yet some seek, and do not at once find

headnotes.la: Vocant enim et clamant, rogant ut de hac carne liberentur, et non exaudit eos Dominus
headnotes.en: For they call and cry out, they beg to be freed from this flesh, and the Lord does not hear them

headnotes.la: Civitas Ecclesia, custodes apostoli; custodes, inquam, apostoli et doctores, qui circum Ecclesiam vadunt, qui eam ab inimicis defendunt,
headnotes.en: The city is the Church, the keepers the apostles; the keepers, I say, the apostles and doctors, who go about the Church, who defend her from her enemies,

headnotes.la: videlicet gladio spiritus
headnotes.en: namely with the sword of the spirit

headnotes.la: timore videlicet compunctionis, et amoris, et sententiis Scripturarum, quae quasi sagittae acutissimae inimicorum fugant exercitum
headnotes.en: namely with the fear of compunction and of love, and with the sayings of the Scriptures, which like the sharpest arrows put the army of the enemies to flight

headnotes.la: … inquit, pallium, pravam voluntatem et vitiorum multitudinem, qua involuta et cooperta eram, apostoli et doctores mihi tulerunt, et vestimento fidei, veste candida et nuptiali me induerunt. Apostropha
headnotes.en: …depraved will and the multitude of vices in which I was wrapped and covered — the apostles and doctors took from me, and clothed me with the garment of faith, with a white and nuptial robe. Apostrophe

headnotes.la: Vox Synagogae
headnotes.en: The voice of the Synagogue

headnotes.la: Nobilior nobilium, fortior fortium, sapientior sapientium. Qualis, inquam, est, dic qualis est,
headnotes.en: More noble than the noble, stronger than the strong, wiser than the wise. What manner of one, I say, is he? Say what manner of one he is,

headnotes.la: ut tuum ei amorem nuntiaremus. Vox Ecclesiae
headnotes.en: — that we might announce thy love to him. The voice of the Church

headnotes.la: Candidus quidem, quia nulla vitiorum macula eum decoloravit. Rubicundus autem, quia proprio sanguine cruentatus est. Juxta illud
headnotes.en: White indeed, because no stain of vices has discoloured him; but ruddy, because he was made bloody with his own blood. According to that word

headnotes.la: [n: (Isa. LXIII, 1.)]
headnotes.en: [n: (Isa. LXIII, 1.)]

headnotes.la: id est ex omni multitudine angelorum et hominum
headnotes.en: that is, out of the whole multitude of angels and of men

headnotes.la: [n: (Psal. LXXXVIII, 7.)]
headnotes.en: [n: (Psal. LXXXVIII, 7.)]

headnotes.la: Quid per caput, nisi divinitas? Unde Apostolus
headnotes.en: What by the head, but the divinity? Whence the Apostle

headnotes.la: …bus omnibus praefertur. Non enim factura factori, creatura Creatori aequiparari potest. Duae namque naturae sunt in Christo, quarum altera est aurum, altera vero terra; divinitas scilicet et humanitas
headnotes.en: … thing made cannot be made equal to its maker, nor the creature to the Creator. For there are two natures in Christ, of which the one is gold and the other earth: namely, the divinity and the humanity

headnotes.la: …lium multitudines elatae palmarum, quoniam semper ad altiora festinant, viriditatem non amittunt, siccari et mori non possunt, et de virtute in virtutem crescentes, coelos ascendunt. De quibus dicitur
headnotes.en: … the high boughs of palms, since they always hasten to higher things, do not lose their greenness, cannot be dried up or die, and, growing from virtue to virtue, ascend the heavens. Of whom it is said

headnotes.la: Hi autem Christi comae dicuntur, quoniam ejus fidei, quae omnium virorum caput est, firmiter inhaerent
headnotes.en: And these are called Christ's locks, since they cleave firmly to his faith, which is the head of all men

headnotes.la: Quare nigrae? Quia macerantur, tribulantur, aestum et multas adversitates patiuntur. Unde superius dixit
headnotes.en: Why black? Because they are worn down, they are afflicted, they suffer the heat and many adversities. Whence she said above

headnotes.la: id est casti et simplices, non elati, non ira confusi. Per oculos autem Spiritus sancti gratias intelligimus, quibus sancti illuminantur. Unde est illud
headnotes.en: that is, chaste and simple, not lifted up, not confounded with anger. And by the eyes we understand the graces of the Holy Spirit, by which the saints are enlightened. Whence is that word

headnotes.la: Possumus autem et per oculos patriarchas et prophetas intelligere, quibus ipse Dominus ait
headnotes.en: And we may also understand by the eyes the patriarchs and prophets, to whom the Lord himself says

headnotes.la: subauditur, existentes. Sunt namque apostoli et doctores super aquarum rivos, quando in Scripturarum voluminibus exercentur
headnotes.en: — understand: being there. For the apostles and doctors are upon the rivers of waters when they are exercised in the volumes of the Scriptures

headnotes.la: Aliter enim simplices et parvuli eas bibere non possunt. Ergo quia lacte sunt lotae, et sapientes, et insipientes eis utuntur, quoniam omnis scientiae in se continent principatum
headnotes.en: …le and the little ones cannot drink them. Therefore, because they are washed with milk, both the wise and the unwise make use of them, since they contain in themselves the sovereignty of all knowledge
